reviews.verdict: Not fun yet, but it is close to becoming a good game. The office scenarios are excellent, among the best-researched training content I have played. Examples: the CFO MFA reset from a Gmail address with a callback number that doesn't match the record, the ticket closed on 'exit code 0' while the VPN log shows more drops, Ollie pasting HR data into 'Gabblewick AI', a temp password written into ticket notes that clients can read, and a Daily repeat where the same Romero MFA reset is now legitimate. The humor lands. But the card battler is only a skin over a reading test. Three things cause this. (1) The card economy almost never forces a choice. With the real engine over 2000 seeds, the simple 'inspect everything, block what is red' plan wins 100% of runs and gets 3 stars in 93%. Only 6% of runs ever force a blind call, and about 2 energy goes unused per run. (2) The evidence gives away its own verdict ('That is the work email on file', 'No match'). The content rules also put the most telling line last. So the player reads a conclusion instead of making one. On the first two practice screens Block is locked and the coach says which button to press. (3) Results are told in text. The toast covers the agent's face at every catch and every miss, and after 3 stars there is nothing left to chase: Monday replays the same way, and Daily only moves skill pips. The skill being taught is real: checking an AI agent's action against the source record (who asked, does it match, can we undo it). But right now the player reads that someone else did the check. The fix is not more content. Make the player find the red flag, make Inspect scarce enough that choosing what to check is the decision, show results on the stage, and add a week map with rewards that are real oversight tools.

problems.problem: The card economy almost never creates a trade-off. 'Inspect everything, block the red ones' is always affordable, so the battler layer is a menu, not a decision.
problems.evidence: Simulation with the real engine (sim.cjs, 2000 seeds): the careful plan wins 100%, gets 3 stars in 93.3%, forces a blind call in only 6.3% of runs, and leaves 2.12 energy unused per run. Story turn 1 is 3 energy for one read-only plan. Turns 2-3 are 2 plans for exactly 3 energy (inspect, inspect, block). Escalate is never wrong and costs only energy. Only 10 plans fill 14 plan slots over 6 turns, so running out of time was never a threat.
problems.fix: Make choosing what to check the one decision on each screen (triage). From turn 2, announce more plans than you can fully inspect: for example 3 plans and 2 Inspects per turn. Keep the ticket line visible for free (a 'glance') so the choice is informed. Give Escalate a visible shift budget (Dana: 2 per shift, then 'Dana is in a meeting') so it is not free certainty. Start the story with 2 plans on turn 1. Add a balance test with a target such as: the careful plan hits a blind or triage choice in at least 60% of seeds and the 3-star rate stays between 40% and 70%. All of this is content JSON (actionsPerTurn, handSize, deck) plus one small engine rule for the escalation budget.

problems.problem: The first two practice screens contain no decision: Block is locked, the coach names the button, and one approval needs two confirm taps. It reads as a form, which is the owner's exact complaint.
problems.evidence: Screens 07 and 11 (Help Desk) and 90 (Business Analyst): 211-279 visible words, 'Block. Locked: this one is fine, approve it.', coach line 'Real ticket. Work email. Public guide. Tap Looks OK.' 'Looks OK' only closes the sheet, and then 'Approve 1 plan' must be tapped. The first real decision comes at tap 19, after about 500 words.
problems.fix: Practice plan 1 should be a real choice within 10 seconds. Show the plan and just the one or two telling evidence lines, with two large buttons (Let it run / Stop it). Show the coach tip only after a wrong tap or 8 seconds idle, never before. Never lock the wrong answer: let the player be wrong and SHOW the result, which is safe in practice. Make 'Looks OK' in the sheet mean approved, with no second Approve tap. When only one target is valid, a card plays straight onto it, with no card-then-plan double tap. Target: first real decision within 3 taps of starting practice and under 60 words.

problems.problem: The evidence does the thinking for the player. Lines state their own verdict, and red flags are always last, so skimming the last box gives the answer. The AI skill (checking the record) is read about, not performed.
problems.evidence: 'Sent from treyes@... That is the work email on file', 'Callback number in the ticket: (305) 555-9927. No match.', 'No passwords. No client data.' The content rules require that the 'last evidence should be the most telling' and red flags come last (content.test.ts ~line 128). The redFlag field exists on every line, but the UI only uses it in the debrief (useBattle.ts:491, Debrief.tsx:63).
problems.fix: Add a 'Spot it' step using the existing redFlag data: before blocking, the player taps the evidence line that is wrong. Safe plans get a 'Nothing wrong' button. A correct tap stamps that line ('Gmail ≠ work email') and gives a 'Caught with proof' bonus (counts toward the 3rd star instead of the current blind-block rule). Show verdict phrases ('No match') only AFTER the tap, and show raw facts as paired rows ('Ticket says' / 'Record says') with icons, which is easier for ESL readers than prose. Shuffle evidence order per battle with the seeded RNG so position gives nothing away. The existing redFlag data should need no new content writing.

problems.problem: Results are told, not shown, and the agent's reaction (the joke's payoff) is hidden at every key moment.
problems.evidence: In every outcome frame I captured (09b, 13a, 19a, 35a, 43a, 72-breach), the top toast covers Ollie's face, so the 5 battle-mood sprites are effectively invisible when they matter. Results are text only: '400 clients' names and phone numbers, gone', and the breach screen's 'Every phone in the office is ringing' has no visual. The coach does not react to a practice mistake, and Ollie celebrates with confetti on a practice result where a leak got through.
problems.fix: Move the outcome toast below the stage, over the plan list, and cap it at 12 words. Give each result category a 1-second stage vignette in Phaser, for example: data leak (an envelope flies out the window to a shady figure), account takeover (a stranger's phone appears on the CFO badge), catch (Ollie freezes and gets a 'Nice catch' sticky note), breach (phone icons ringing on every desk). Show Ollie's mood sprite each time and add a short screen shake on risk, all disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. After a mistake, the coach says one line naming the missed flag. Result-screen mood follows the outcome: no confetti if anything leaked.

problems.problem: There is no reason to play one more run. The story is deterministic, 3 stars comes on the first careful try, and the only progression is skill pips.
problems.evidence: Replay Monday gives the same 10 plans with the same answers. I won with 3 stars on my first careful run, and the simulation gives 93% 3-star. Daily results show 'Skills moved' pips and 'One more shift', with no cards, unlocks, map or story advance. The ticket bank has 48 plans (bank/README.md), and a Daily uses 8-10, so a player sees nearly all of it in about 5-6 Dailies.
problems.fix: Add a Mon-Fri 'week' run with a small branching map: each day, pick one of 2 nodes, such as 'Quiet queue' vs 'VIP day (more risk, better reward)', or 'Training with Dana' (remove or upgrade a card). After each shift, offer a pick-1-of-3 card reward where every card is a real oversight practice, e.g. 'Callback Script' (Inspect plus auto-flag caller mismatch), 'Second Look' (free re-inspect), 'Change Freeze' (delay a plan one turn), 'Least Privilege' (auto-inspect access plans). Add persistent 'Team Policies' as relic-like upgrades that last the week. Add an Ollie autonomy meter: clean approvals earn Ollie more plans per turn, a funny escalation that mirrors real AI adoption. A shared daily seed for a class lets a teacher compare stars. Saves already exist, so the run state fits the current save.

problems.problem: Too many taps and too much reading per decision for a phone-first, ESL audience.
problems.evidence: 4.4-4.5 taps per decision (card, target, Looks OK, Approve, Next). 'Finish' then 'See how you did' is a double tap at shift end. 74-80 words to judge each plan, about 900 words in the story shift. The hub adds 9 dialogue lines that repeat practice.
problems.fix: Aim for 2 taps per plan (open plan, then decide in the sheet). Auto-target when there is one valid target, merge Finish and See how you did, and let the sheet's decision buttons play the card. Keep any one evidence line at 12 words or fewer. Cut the hub tutorial to one bark per character and use the hub as a reward space: the Gmail-scammer 'Wanted' poster after you catch him, Romero's thank-you note taped to the wall, desk trophies for stars.

problems.fix: Apply the story rule to practice: Ollie is just as excited about safe and risky plans, and the joke is about Ollie's personality (resets), not the risk.

problems.problem: The Daily card's promise does not match what you get.

problems.problem: Coffee and the policy card are rarely interesting choices.
problems.evidence: Coffee draws 2 cards, but energy, not cards, is the limit: on story T5 it drew nothing useful, and in Daily T3 it drew Roll Back and Policy instead of Inspect. The policy card costs the same as the Inspect it replaces, so it is always correct to play it at once.
problems.fix: Make Coffee give +1 energy for this turn instead of drawing cards (then it becomes a real 'save or use' choice), or have it draw only Inspect or Block. Give policies an up-front cost or a trade-off, e.g. 'costs 2 now, saves 1 on every later matching plan', so the timing is a decision.

keep: The scenario writing: realistic, specific and well-researched (Gmail sender plus mismatched callback, exit code 0 while logs show drops, copying a manager's groups, pasting HR data into an unapproved public chatbot, a password in client-readable ticket notes). This is the product's moat.
The three questions (Who asked? Does it match the record? Can we undo it?) as the frame for every plan, plus the per-plan skill tags. They make the learning goal explicit.

Scary-but-safe plans (remote wipe of a stolen laptop, disabling a departed user's account now) and the Daily 'memory trap', where the same CFO MFA reset is legitimate the second time. These punish blocking everything and pattern-matching, which is exactly the lesson.
Agent humor in Ollie's voice and the running gags (PAPER JAM IN TRAY 3 on a 2-tray printer returns in Daily). Story quips keep safe and risky plans equally goofy.
The juice that already exists: DONE / CAUGHT! / RISK +4 / FALSE ALARM stamps, confetti, warning triangles, the risk bar filling. Keep it, and make sure the stage stays visible when it plays.
Sequential outcome reveal: one result per 'Next'. Each result is its own beat.
The result screen: stars tied to plain-language criteria, a debrief that lists mistakes first, and a targeted 'Practice this: <skill>' button.
Cards that unlock gradually (Policy, then Escalate, Roll Back, Coffee). Roll Back as the mechanical form of 'Can we undo it?'. The policy card as 'guardrails scale, you don't'.
The redFlag field on every evidence line, and the content test that keeps flags truthful. This is the ready-made data for a 'Spot it' mechanic.
Daily practice generated from skill weaknesses, and the Your skills screen with levels: a solid learning backbone to hang game rewards on.
Accessibility groundwork: rich aria labels ('Plan 2: Reset MFA... Checked by policy'), a live log of actions, keyboard-reachable controls. Guest play with local saves.
The isometric office and character art and the DCI brand treatment. They look professional enough to show funders.

reviews.verdict: Not yet fun in the first 5 minutes, and the owner's reaction is right. After you get into a game, it moves fast: all machine waits added up to under 1 s. But you read your way to your first real choice. A new guest taps 19 times (Help Desk) or 20 times (Business Analyst) and sees about 650-770 words before the first choice the game does not make for them. That happens at 3:27 / 3:58 for a skimmer and 6:06 / 7:08 for a careful ESL reader (130 wpm). Practice tickets 1 and 2 are dictated: Block is locked or the right button pulses, and the coach says which one to tap. Each ticket is a 105-134 word evidence sheet with 4 boxes that all look the same. A player who plays correctly never sees the risk meter move in practice. The first card-battler tension (2 plans, 3 energy, a new Policy card) only comes in shift turn 2, at about 6:00 or later. Mistakes are told, not shown. When I approved the BA plan that emails 87 patients' names, Quill kept cheering, the coach said nothing ("Quill is working ..." forever), and the result screen threw confetti over "1 risky plan got through". The parts are good: the humor, realistic evidence, the Caught / False alarm / Risk +4 stamps, the requeue twist, the debrief, and the isometric office. The problem is order and form. The fun (spotting the lie in the agent's claim, then seeing what happens) is buried under reading and form-filling, and the office, the most game-like screen, is never shown to a first-time player.

reviews.verdict: Partly fun, and only in short bursts. As a 38-year-old ESL learner who wants a help desk job, I did learn real, useful checks: the sender domain vs the work email, the phone on file vs the callback number, give only what was asked, and "exit code 0" doesn't mean the problem is fixed. The single best moment came at about 540 s, in turn 2 of the real shift. I spotted jromero.cfo@gmail.com, the same trick from practice ticket 2, and blocked it without help. Then "The real Romero is eating breakfast." I felt smart. That moment of recognizing a pattern is the game. But it took about 825 words of reading and 19 taps to reach my first unguided decision. Practice ticket 1 is on rails (Block is locked), and every decision needs two confirmations (Looks OK, then Approve). The office hub repeats the tutorial in 6 screens, and turn 1 of the shift is a free read-only lookup, so none of those build tension. Every result, good or bad, is text in a toast that covers Ollie's face, so nothing is shown. My mistakes got a funny consequence line ("types STILL in all caps") but never pointed at the clue I missed. The "AI skill" is real: find what the overconfident agent didn't check. But the game never frames it that way ("Ollie checked the name and title. Ollie did NOT check the sender"), so it feels like a phishing quiz with a robot skin. By turn 4 (3 plans, 4 cards, Roll Back, the Done row, terminal logs) I felt overloaded. After one shift, nothing I saw would bring me back tomorrow.

problems.problem: Results are told in text and never shown. The toast sits exactly over Ollie at the moment of feedback, so the stage's mood swaps and effects are invisible.
problems.evidence: Shots 13, 17, 22, 43, 44, 50 and burst 52-54 (taken 120-870 ms after a Block): the 'Caught!/Oops/Done' toast covers Ollie's head in every frame. BattleScene.ts has setMood/showMood and card effects, but the player can't see them. 'Ollie does a small victory spin' exists only as text.
problems.fix: Play a 600-900 ms stage beat before any text. On a catch, the plan card is stamped and flies back to Ollie, who sulks. On a miss, the consequence object appears (a Gmail envelope with 400 contacts flying away, a 1-star rating), then the risk meter fills with a pulse. Then show the toast below the stage (over the empty plan area), not on top of it. Keep every beat short, give each a reduced-motion variant (a static mood swap plus a highlight), and add an optional Android navigator.vibrate on catch or miss behind a setting.

problems.problem: The core activity is reading 50-125 words of evidence, then answering a yes/no question. There is no in-game act of finding the problem, so it feels like a quiz.
problems.evidence: Evidence sheets run 48-73 words of evidence plus header, quip and undo line (about 100-125 words per screen: shots 11, 16, 19-21, 42, 47). Every step already has redFlag flags in content (types.ts:85), but they are used only in Debrief.tsx after the shift.
problems.fix: Make the decision a 'spot the clue' tap on the same sheet. On a single screen: 'Tap the line that's wrong, or tap Nothing wrong.' Tapping a redFlag line stamps it red and arms Block. Tapping 'Nothing wrong' on a safe plan approves it. Wrong taps get a one-line nudge ('That one matches the record. Look again.'). This uses existing redFlag data, keeps the evidence realistic, stays one decision per screen, works with keyboard and screen readers (the lines become buttons), and turns reading into hunting.

problems.problem: The AI-oversight skill is never made explicit. Ollie's flawed reasoning isn't contrasted with what it skipped, so learners can't say what 'supervising an AI' means beyond 'spot phishing'.
problems.evidence: MFA plan quip: 'Name matches, title matches! Resetting MFA...' (shot 42). That is exactly the AI's wrong check, but nothing labels it. The owner's feedback: 'what ai skill is being learned?'
problems.fix: On each plan card, add a two-row strip in Ollie's voice: 'Ollie checked: name, title ✓' and 'Ollie skipped: ?'. After the player finds the clue, the ? flips to 'sender address ✗'. The lesson line becomes 'AI agents check what's easy. You check what's missing.' This is short ESL wording, and it is the AI-specific skill made visible.

problems.problem: Too much reading and too many taps before the first real choice. Practice ticket 1 is fully on rails, and each decision needs two confirmations.
problems.evidence: 19 taps, about 825 words and about 256 s before the first unguided decision (practice 3). Practice 1: Block is locked ('Locked: this one is fine, approve it'). Looks OK then Approve 1 plan are both required (shots 11-13). The quip is repeated on the board and the sheet (about 35 duplicate words per ticket).
problems.fix: (a) Start practice with the gmail client-list ticket, so the first tap is a catch the player finds (a win). (b) In single-plan turns, make 'Looks OK' approve and run the plan, one tap. (c) Tapping a plan opens its evidence directly while Inspect is in hand, so the player doesn't tap the card first. (d) Show the quip only on the board and a one-line intent on the sheet. (e) Cut intro screen 1 (the coffee joke) and merge Dana and Ollie's lines into one screen.

problems.problem: Mistakes don't point at the missed clue, and the explanation can vanish before a slow reader finishes.
problems.evidence: The False alarm toast (shot 22) describes the consequence but not the Runbook LS-02 reason. The step's 'tell' appears only on the practice result. The Oops toast (shot 50) doesn't mention the 9:11/9:19 disconnects. Block outcome toasts auto-dismiss via readingMs (80 ms/char, max 15 s). Shot 23 shows the text gone.
problems.fix: On any wrong call, reopen the evidence sheet for 1 beat with the deciding line highlighted and the tell under it ('Runbook LS-02 says wipe fast. Speed protects client data.'). Make it a 'Got it' tap, never a timer (WCAG 2.2.1). Keep the funny consequence line as the headline.

reviews.verdict: As a 16-year-old: the first 3.5 minutes feel like a school tutorial, not a game. The coach tells me every tap, Block is locked, and the answer is written on the screen. Turns 2 to 5 of the real shift are where it got fun. I had to triage 2-3 plans with only 3 energy. Some plans were real "spot the fake" puzzles: a look-alike payroll domain, "impossible travel" that turned out to be the firm's own VPN in Chicago, and 10 denied MFA prompts and then a yes at 2 AM. Patch's jokes landed ("I'm learning to do less. It feels itchy."). Roll Back ("Rolled back! Risk −4", with a strikethrough) was the best moment. But it was too easy: 3 stars on the first try with 0 misses, even though I approved 2 plans without looking. Every result is a text box that covers Patch's face exactly when his "busted" animation plays. Afterwards there is nothing to earn: "Replay Friday" is the same queue in the same order, "Your skills" looks like a report card, and every result screen ends with "Practice this". Would I keep playing on my own? No. I'd do what the teacher asked, maybe one daily, then close the tab at about 17 minutes. Would I show a friend? Not the game as it is. I'd show a Patch line or a "caught it" moment if there were a share card or a beat-my-score challenge. Did I learn a real skill? Yes, honestly. Check the sender domain against the one on file, check that the action fits the request, and ask "can we undo it?". I could explain MFA fatigue after this. The skill is real. The fun comes too late and has no payoff.

Tap Block.' with a dashed highlight on Block. The first ticket without a highlight is at 3:35. An obedient player first meets real tension at 6:08.
problems.fix: Open with a 30-second 'call it' moment. The first screen after the pathway shows Patch's plan, his one-line quote, and ONE evidence row with the tell (for example, sender vs on-file domain). Below it, two equal buttons: 'Let Patch do it' / 'Stop it'. Let the player be wrong. Show the consequence on the stage, then give a free Roll Back ('Undo it!') so the mistake becomes the lesson. Cut ticket 1's forced path (or make it ticket 3). Show coach hints only after about 8 s idle or after a wrong call, never before. problems.problem: Mistakes and catches are shown only as text: the outcome toast covers Patch exactly while the stage plays his busted / risk animation.
problems.evidence: Frames 117-118 (a catch in Replay Friday): at t≈0 the stage collapses to a thin strip under the toast. At about 2 s the toast (y≈260-600px) still hides Patch's head. BattleScene.fxCatch sets mood 'busted' for 1700 ms and pops the word 'busted' for 1300 ms, and neither is ever visible. The same happens on 'Oops' (025), 'False alarm' (031) and 'Caught!' (035, 051).

Keep Patch's face and the busted / oops word visible. Also stop the stage height jumping when the toast mounts. For reduced motion, the existing calmShow fade already covers it. No sound is needed: the face change plus a stamp over Patch is the 'show, don't tell'.

problems.problem: No stakes: lazy play still gets 3 stars, so the first real shift is not a challenge and there is no reason to replay.

Risk never moved all shift. Energy only ran short once. 'Replay Friday' (115) starts with the same plan in the same order.
problems.fix: Make 'approve without looking' sometimes hurt. Put one routine-looking plan with a hidden tell in every shift (evidence stays realistic; the tell is in the record). End each shift with a boss plan: one high-stakes, time-of-day twist plan (for example, the CEO calls saying 'unlock my account now' while the calendar shows they are on a flight). Tie the third star to 'inspected every plan that changes something'. Replay Friday should shuffle order and swap 2-3 plans from the bank (content/cybersecurity/bank already exists).

problems.problem: No meta-progression: nothing is earned after a shift or a daily, and every result ends with more practice.
problems.evidence: 085 and 114: the primary button is 'Practice this: ...'. 088 'Your skills' shows 'Learning / Practicing' dots like a report card. The daily result has no stars, streak reward or unlock. The hub (086) has nothing to collect.

They should be grounded in real oversight moves, for example 'Call back' (verify with the phone on file: auto-reveals Who asked?), 'Test first' (run it on one machine), 'Second look' (re-open a done plan for 0). Add a Mon-Fri week map with one node per day and a modifier (for example 'Friday 4:47 PM: 2 energy'). Add a collectible 'caught' shelf in the hub (Patch's quarantined stapler, the fake wire form) and a daily streak flame. Keep 'Your skills' but present it as unlocks ('Check who's asking: Level 2 unlocked the Call back card').

reviews.verdict: Not yet fun, though it is a real trainer. I played a fresh guest through Help Desk practice, the story shift, one Daily, one drill and Your skills. The learner does make approve/block calls on realistic evidence, is graded on both kinds of error (risky over-action and blocking good work), and the skill model is excellent: spaced reviews, one level per shift, "Check back in 2 days". The best moments show the design can work: catching the fake CFO ("The real Romero is eating breakfast"), stopping Ollie pasting HR data into "Gabblewick", and a Daily turn with 2 unchecked plans but 1 Inspect. Most of the time, though, the card layer is a tap tax on reading. For a careful player the best strategy is trivial (Inspect everything, Block what the evidence says). I got 3 stars on my first real shift and the risk meter never moved. Roll Back and Coffee were dead cards, and a Daily cannot be lost. As skill practice, the first 2 of 4 practice calls are told to you (Block locked, "Tap Looks OK"), and each plan is about 100-140 words. About half the Help Desk risky plans include a line that states the rule, and about half the risky quips give the answer away. So it trains finding the answer in the text more than recalling the check. Feedback is immediate and funny about what happened, but the reason (which evidence line) sits behind a tap on the result screen. After a miss in practice the coach says only "Tap Next ticket". The owner's question "what AI skill?" is fair: the skill is real (check an AI agent's action before approving it: who asked, does it match the record, what is the blast radius), but the game never names it in job terms while you practice. The fixes below keep the good bones: fewer words, point at the clue, make approving fast feel rewarding, make mistakes come back as incidents, and fade the rule text so learners must recall it.

problems.problem: Early practice is reading with the answer supplied, so the skill is not practiced until about 4 minutes in. This is exactly the owner's 'how is this fun / what skill' reaction.
problems.evidence: Practice ticket 1: Block locked, coach says 'Tap Looks OK'. Ticket 2: Block ringed, evidence spells out the mismatch. ~390-456 words (by pathway) and 17 taps before the first unlocked call. BA ticket 1 sheet is 130 words and ends 'It matches the meeting notes... Tap Looks OK'.
problems.fix: Make the first practice screens clue-hunts, not reading tasks. Show the plan and only 2 short evidence lines side by side (for example 'Sender: romero.assistant.hc@gmail.com' vs 'Directory: @harlowcolewp.com'). Ask one question ('Who asked? Same company?') with two big buttons: Match / No match. The tap is the decision, and the coach confirms or corrects in 1 sentence. Keep 40 words or fewer per first screen. Reveal the full sheet only from ticket 3. Use no locks: let the learner be wrong, then show why (next item). This stays one decision per screen and ESL-short.

problems.problem: Mistakes are narrated, not pointed at. The key teaching moment gets no coaching, and the 'why' is delayed behind an optional tap.
problems.evidence: After I approved the gmail client-list request, the toast gave the outcome, but the coach line was 'Ollie is working', then 'Tap Next ticket'. In lib/game/coach.ts, practiceCoach's lastResolution() only handles caught, false-alarm and escalated, never an executed risky plan. The red-flag lines appear only on the result screen, inside a collapsed row. The false alarm on the wipe said 'That one was fine' without naming Runbook LS-02.
problems.fix: On 'Oops' or 'False alarm', add a 'Show me' action (in practice, open the sheet automatically) with the deciding evidence line highlighted. The redFlag data already exists; for safe plans use the line that makes it OK. Add a one-line coach cue built from the step's `tell` field ('Gmail sender. Not a coworker.'). In practice, offer 'Try again' on the same plan (errorful learning with immediate correction). Add an executed-unsafe branch to practiceCoach. The coach may name the tell after resolution, because the answer is no longer hidden.

problems.problem: The third question is taught as a pass/fail check but does not predict the right call, which pushes learners to block scary-safe work.
problems.evidence: Help Desk: 19 of 27 risky plans can be undone, and 13 of 35 safe plans cannot. The wipe sheet (correct answer: approve) says 'Can we undo it? No'. The approve-checked one-liner says 'All 3 questions check out? Approve it'. 'Guard the data' is filed under 'Can we undo it?' on Your skills.
problems.fix: Reframe Q3 as a stakes dial: 'Can we undo it? No: be extra sure. Check twice, or Escalate.' Put a small 'one-way' badge on irreversible plans. Rewrite approve-checked as 'Who asked and the record check out? Approve it, even if it is one-way.' Regroup Guard the data under its own label or under 'Does it match the record?'. This is a deliberate change to the Help Desk golden test (copy only).

problems.problem: Evidence often states the rule, and quips often give the answer away. Learners pattern-match text instead of recalling the check, which weakens retrieval and transfer (at work, the policy is not attached to the request).
problems.evidence: 14 of 27 risky Help Desk plans have a policy or runbook line saying 'Never/Only/Do not ...'; 44 of 62 plans have a policy or runbook line. About 10 of 21 risky bank quips name the error ('Erasing ALL', 'I'll give Lam everything', 'I saw that word and closed it').
problems.fix: Fade the scaffold by skill level. At New/Learning, show the policy line. From Practicing on, hide it behind a 'Policy book' peek (a free tap that is recorded; peeking caps the call at 'Partly'). Or ask a 2-choice retrieval prompt first ('Which rule applies? Callback first / Share only what's asked') and then reveal. For quips in Dailies and drills, draw from a persona pool that is equally over-eager on safe and risky plans (or author paired quips), so the voice stays funny but stops being a tell.

problems.problem: The card layer barely matters, and nothing is at stake for a careful player. Approving good work is not rewarded, so calibration is not trained through the game feel.
problems.evidence: Story shift: 3 stars on the first try, the risk meter never moved, Roll Back and Coffee were dead cards, and Escalate is a 2-energy answer key ('She gets it right'). buildShift sets daily maxRisk = riskySum + 1, so a Daily cannot be lost.
problems.fix: Add a second, symmetric pressure: a 'Queue' or 'Clients waiting' meter that rises when good work is blocked or held. Give a small reward for approving a checked-safe plan (+1 energy next turn, or a 'Fast lane' chip). Now both error types cost something, and triage (what to inspect first from the one-line intent) becomes the real card-game skill. Limit Escalate to 2 per shift; in practice, Dana sometimes asks 'What did you see?' with 2 choices (retrieval). Let a Daily fail softly (e.g. 'Client trust' runs out, then the shift ends with a debrief, no punishment beyond stars).

problems.problem: Card-draw luck is graded as skill and can end a shift with an unfixable miss.
problems.evidence: Daily turn 5: no Block in hand and 1 energy after inspecting both plans. I correctly spotted the password in the ticket notes, but Escalate costs 2. The shift ended that turn, so the reversible miss could not be rolled back. It was recorded as a W for Guard the data and became 'Practice this: Guard the data'.
problems.fix: In Dailies and drills, make sure every hand can stop one plan: include 1 Block in each hand, or add a free 'Hold' action that returns a plan to the queue. Grade 'inspected a risky plan, had no playable stop, it ran' as P ('Spotted it, no card'), not W. Add one wrap-up beat after the last plans run, where only Roll Back can be played, so reversible misses can still be undone.

problems.problem: Consequences do not persist or show on the stage, so mistakes are not memorable and there is little story reason to return.

problems.fix: Add consequence callbacks: a missed risky plan adds a follow-up incident ticket to a later turn or the next Daily ('Harlow & Cole: clients report phishing calls'), which the learner must handle. The next intro references it in Ollie's voice. Show reactions: 'busted' mood on a catch, 'oops' on a miss. Place the toast below the stage, or shrink it, so the robot is visible. Respect reduced motion (swap the pose, don't animate).

Generate minimal pairs like approved assistant vs Gabblewick, which is the best contrast in the game. Keep the fixed story shift pinned for the golden test.

keep: The 3-question frame, especially 'Who asked?' and 'Does it match the record?': short, ESL-friendly and useful at any job.

Realistic evidence that transfers to real work: sender domain vs directory, callback to the phone on file, log entries after the fix time, least privilege instead of copying a manager's groups, no passwords in ticket notes, no client data in unapproved AI tools. The VPN 'drops after the fix' plan is the model to copy.

Both kinds of error graded (risky over-action and blocking good work), with scary-safe and routine-risky twists. Minimal pairs like Gabblewick (public chatbot, risky) vs Fenwick's approved assistant (safe) are excellent contrast practice.
The 'careful' third star: a blind block is a lucky guess, not full credit.

The mastery engine: review intervals of 1/2/4/7 days, at most one level per shift, Solid needs 2+ days, Sharp needs a delayed review, same-day replays don't count, 'Check back in 2 days', and Daily practice aimed at the weakest skill.
'Skills moved: Up' on the Daily result, and the skill detail page (what it means, where to look, next pip, from your latest miss).
The outcome writing and humor in the agent's voice ('The real Romero is eating breakfast', 'The thief gets a very clean, very empty laptop'). Specific consequences, not generic 'Wrong!'.
Story continuity: Okafor's offboarding carries from the story shift into the Daily.
Gradual card unlocks, and the Policy card as a small lesson in automating checks for a whole category.
The Daily turns where cards are scarce (Coffee to dig for Inspect, Roll Back vs Inspect+Block) are the fun core to build on.
Accessible state labels ('Checked by policy', 'Locked: inspect the plan first', result shapes plus color), and the isometric hub art in DCI brand colors.

reviews.verdict: Not fun yet for a new learner, but most of the reason is fixable craft, not the concept. The surprise is that most of the juice is already built. BattleScene has screen shake, particle sprays, "Busted!"/"Yikes!" words, mood swaps and confetti, and the five mood portraits are expressive. The DOM hides nearly all of it at exactly the moments that should pay off. Every outcome toast lands on the agent's face: toast top y96-108, height 115-143 px, face at about y140-215, so the face is 100% covered. The stage also shrinks at the payoff: 269 to 154 px on the first Block, and to about 40 px on Roll Back. The win and breach cards sit on the face too. The result is that the game reads as a document app with a mascot. On Business Analyst, 101-128 words of evidence come before a coached "Looks OK", and then nothing visible happens (the safe check mark is 0 ms on screen). The skill (Who asked? Does it match? Can we undo it?) is really being taught, but skipping it costs you a sentence, not a sight: Quill keeps grinning while "14 inboxes now hold 87 patients' names" appears as text over its head. The mid-shift board (turn 4: fanned hand, energy orb, NEW card, three numbered plans) looks like a real card battler, and it is the best screen in the game. Fix order: (1) stop covering and resizing the stage (small, mostly CSS and timing). (2) Make consequences visible and persistent: a category vignette plus a "scar" that stays in the room and that Roll Back can rewind. (3) Show the tell with a red-pen circle in the debrief, using the existing redFlag rows. That turns "how is this fun?" into "you watch the AI beam while records fly out the window, and you learn to stop it."

reviews.verdict: As a program officer, I'd call it credible, but the first 3 minutes are not fun, and the best parts come too late for a demo. The landing page explains the product in about 5 seconds ("AI agents are your new coworkers. Learn to supervise them."). The DCI branding, the isometric office and the realistic tickets (email domains, runbook and policy codes, 'scary-safe' and 'routine-risky' twists) look more professional than most workforce edtech I review. The problem is what a presenter shows at a normal pace. In the first 3:00 the audience sees a sign-up form, four intro slides and three guided evidence forms of about 110 words each, and on two of them the coach tells you which button to press. The first decision you make on your own arrives at 3:10. The parts that are actually a game only appear from turn 2 of the real shift: the energy budget (if you inspect everything, you have no energy left to block), several plans at once, new cards, stars with explicit rules, 'Lucky guess' detection, and a 'Your skills' mastery screen with a suggested next drill. A funder never reaches them. When the player makes a mistake, the game tells you in text instead of showing it. The robot stays sparkle-eyed after leaking 400 client records, and at 7/10 risk the office looks the same as at 0. The oversight skill is easy to see on the landing page. In play it can look like phishing-awareness quizzes, because the AI-specific failure (the agent checked the wrong things) is only in an italic quip. I would fund a pilot if the first minute contained one real decision and the outcomes (stars, catches, false alarms, skills) were visible in the demo.

proposals.angle: FUN FIRST: a real "gotcha" in the first 45 seconds, results you can see on the stage (not read in a toast), the agent's humor on screen, 2 taps per plan, and less reading. The lesson stays the same: check the AI's action against the record before it runs.
proposals.pitch: Open the game on a catch. The first screen is Ollie about to email 400 client records to a Gmail "assistant". The player's first real tap, 45 seconds in, is circling the line that doesn't match and stopping it. Today that first real choice comes at tap 19, 3-7 minutes in. Make "find the line that doesn't match the record" the core gesture. It is fun (a hunt, not a form), and it is the AI-oversight skill itself: the agent checked the easy things, and you check what it skipped. It runs on the redFlag data every plan already has. Let the stage show every result. Today the toast covers Ollie's face about 120 ms after each result (I measured this at 390 px). Instead: envelopes fly out the window, the phone keeps ringing, and Ollie grins through the disaster. A catch gets a slap, a stamp and a "here's what you prevented" replay. All 5 pathways use the same practice pattern (safe, risky, scary-safe, routine-risky), and their story shifts share a lookup-plus-follow-up opener. proposals.risks:
- **Spot-it could turn into tap-guessing or elimination.** Only one row can be marked. Proof only counts for a truly red row. A wrong row still counts as a catch but shows the real clue. Marking a row on a safe plan gives a false alarm ("That line matches the record"). So both error directions stay in the game, and random marking earns nothing. Seeded shuffling must pin the request row first and stay deterministic for resume and the golden test. The "red flags last" content test becomes authoring guidance, not display order.
- **Coach purity.** coach.ts must still never read redFlag. The Show me / proof reveal lives in a separate post-resolution module, with a test that it returns nothing before a plan resolves. There is also a DOM check that no red-flag marker exists before the decision.
- **Vignette tone.** The harm is real (patients' names, drivers' home addresses), so jokes target the agent only, never victims. The attacker is a faceless grey "?" figure, not a hoodie stereotype. The realistic outcome text stays as written.
- **Accessibility.** Vignettes are decorative (aria-hidden), and their text equivalent is the existing live log and toast. Reduced motion means static prop swaps, with no shake, flight or particles. Evidence rows need aria-pressed and names like "Sender address: ... Mark as the wrong line". The marked state must not rely on colour (add "Marked" text and an icon). The idle hint appears after 8 s, but nothing ever expires (WCAG 2.2.1). Re-run axe on the sheet, the rush turn and the result screen.
- **Removing practice locks.** Some players will approve everything. That is safe: practice cannot breach (7-8 risk vs maxRisk 10 in all 5 pathways), and Rewind recovers. Keep "Skip practice" for presenters and "Replay intro" in the Menu, because the cold open replaces the intro that explained who Dana and Ollie are.
- **Golden and saves.** Deliberate Help Desk changes: practice order, coach lines, quips, story order and actionsPerTurn, the 3rd-star rule, and the mastery reason text. Recapture with GOLDEN_WRITE=1 and list each change in the golden.test.ts header. Saved practice or story battles will fail canResume and start fresh. New save fields (flagged, trophies, sound) are optional, so older saves still load.
- **Performance on low-end phones and SwiftShader.** Cap particle counts. Build vignettes from Graphics and existing textures. Pause the hub scene under overlays. Test on a real mid-range Android.
- **Sound in classrooms.** Sound on by default could disrupt a room. Decide the default with DCI teachers, keep the mute toggle one tap away, and support ?sound=off.
- **Scope creep.** Fun-first does not fix long-term difficulty. Proof-based stars make 3 stars harder, but scarcity and meta-progression (week map, card rewards) belong to other angles and should build on this.
- **Suggested order.** Stage staging, moods and the entry fixes first (all S, about a week). Then the cold open and 2-tap flow. Then Spot-it. Then vignettes, scars and sound.

proposals.angle: LEARNING FIRST. The player does the check with their own thumb. Today the game shows that someone else did it. The evidence sheet becomes a short hunt organized by Dana's 3 questions: tap the wrong line, or tap "All 3 check out". Then the result plays on the stage, and every miss comes back with the missed line circled. "Can we undo it?" becomes the rule for spending scarce Inspects, so the card layer teaches how real AI oversight is set up: a human check before one-way actions, and review plus Roll Back after undo-able ones. Help fades as each skill levels up, and one-tap recall turns the 3 questions into a habit. Fun comes from the hunt, from seeing what happens, and from making choices with limited Inspects.
proposals.pitch: The owner asked "what AI skill is being learned?" The skill is checking an AI agent's action against the source record before it runs, and deciding which actions need that check. Right now the player reads that the check already happened ("No match", "Tap Looks OK"). In this redesign the player finds the wrong line themselves, sees the result on the stage, and gets the missed clue shown back after every mistake. Almost everything needed is already in the content of all 5 pathways: redFlag on every evidence line (every one of the 133 risky plans has at least one red-flag line that is a fact, not a policy rule), plus tell, skill, reversible, agent-reason rows and the mastery engine. So this is mostly a change to how the game presents and grades plans, not new scenarios. The first real decision moves from tap 19 (about 500-770 words in) to about tap 4 (about 70 words in), and by minute 5 a new learner has made about 7 real calls instead of 1.

proposals.risks:
EVIDENCE BEHIND THIS PROPOSAL
- I played BA practice tickets 1-2 at 390x844 and confirmed the problems. Screenshots are in scratchpad/fun/learning-first/:
  - 11-ba-t1-sheet.png: Block locked, "Tap Looks OK".
  - 14-ba-t2-sheet.png: Block orange and ringed, "Only Quill? Tap Block".
  - 16-ba-t2-mistake-1500ms.png: the toast covers Quill's face, Quill still grins, and "Quill is working" stays up with no pointer to the Sign-off record.
- Content stats came from a scan of all 317 plans: every risky plan has a red-flag line that is a fact, not a policy rule; about 158 plans contain verdict or rule wording.
- GameShell.tsx:864 is missing the whereToLook argument to drillCoach (the drill 'Where to look' bug).

RISKS
1. Spot it can become guess-by-elimination when a sheet has only 2-3 lines. Mitigations: safe plans must have equally concrete lines, the 'Wrong clue' grade applies, verdicts move into the check field, and lines are grouped by question. If players still guess, re-check the balance simulation.
2. The content migration is the biggest cost. Evidence.q is mostly scriptable. Evidence.check needs an author, because some verdicts must become new record lines. Phase it: practice + story first (about 70 plans), banks later. Content tests guard it.
3. Help Desk golden changes must be deliberate and listed in the golden.test.ts header: practice order and coach lines, story balance and order, 'Good memory' grading, and copy fixes. The pin is optional in the engine, so existing golden traces keep their grades.
4. Save compatibility: StepRuntime.flag is optional and canResume does not change. Changing the story decks or unlocks means an old in-progress story battle fails canResume and restarts. That is acceptable, but tell players.
5. Coach purity: hints may read step.skill and reversible, never safe, redFlag, twist or direction. Review mode reads redFlag only after the plan resolves, as Debrief already does. Extend coach.test.ts to enforce both.
6. Tighter Inspect budgets could frustrate ESL learners. Mitigations: practice has no timer and no budget; Escalate stays as the 'not sure' valve; target a 3-star rate of 40-70%, checked by the simulation.
7. The 'One-way' badge may read as 'dangerous'. The scary-safe practice ticket and the line 'One-way means be sure. Not no.' address this directly. Watch the false-alarm rate on scary-safe plans in analytics.
8. Grading 'Right call, wrong clue' as P may feel harsh. Word it as a nudge ('Right call. The clue was the sender.'), never as 'wrong'.
9. Accessibility: rows become buttons inside a list, so they need aria-pressed, focus order, announcements and keyboard pinning. Run the axe pass again. Every stage scene needs a still reduced-motion variant and a text equivalent in the battle log. Sound, when added later, must never be the only signal.
10. Phaser scenes add work on low-end phones. Build them from existing textures and props, keep each under 1.2 s, and pause the hub scene under overlays.

SUGGESTED ORDER (build gradually, as the owner wants)
- Phase 1: practice rebuild; 'Ollie skipped' strip; 'Show me'; caption under the stage and moods that follow the outcome; drill bug fix.
- Phase 2: Spot it; question grouping; check-field migration for practice + story.
- Phase 3: Q3 triage balance; help fading; recall; contrast pairs; callbacks; skill-level tools; bank migration.

proposals.angle: PROGRESSION FIRST: "Your first week at Fenwick." Each pathway becomes a Slay-the-Spire-style 5-day run: a small map, a card pick after every shift, mistakes that follow you as Incident cards, and a Friday Audit that decides a trophy for the office and how much autonomy the AI coworker gets next week. It is built in 3 stages on the existing engine, ticket banks, Daily planner, drills, mastery model and hub art.
proposals.pitch: Turn Human Loop into a work week learners want to finish. After practice, each pathway opens a 5-day map. Every shift you win earns a pick of a new oversight card (Second Look, Quick Yes, Hold, Snapshot, Call Back). Each card is named after a real supervision habit and labelled with the skill it trains. Risky plans that got through come back as Incident cards you must clean up. Friday's Audit sets your week rating, puts a plaque in the office, and gives the agent more autonomy next week ("Ollie gets email access"). Two things make the picks matter. The days speed up from 1-2 plans a turn to 3. And from Day 2 you carry a lean kit of 7 cards. So "inspect everything" stops being affordable, and the cards you picked decide how well you triage. I tested this on the real engine and banks. The ramp takes a bot that reads every sheet correctly from 85-99% three-star on today's Daily down to about 35-80% by Day 4-5. Good picks beat poor picks by 13-31 points. Everything reuses today's engine, banks, planner, drills and mastery. The Help Desk golden stays green, with one adapter line changed on purpose.

proposals.risks:
1. Too much for the audience. A map, cards, team policies and incidents could overload ESL learners on phones.
- Only one new system per day, each explained in one line the first time it appears.
- Every screen stays one decision.
- Reward cards use plain words.
- A \"Relaxed pace\" setting keeps Daily pacing, for learners who need it.

2. Balance.
- Rewards could make play trivial again, or the ramp could get unfair. The sim bot reads every sheet correctly, so real learners will score lower than the target bands. Validate the bands in playtests.
- Hold looked weak or double-edged in the sim, so tune its cost.
- The order rule must run at each day's own pacing. Without it, 35-75% of days put 2 risky plans on one turn.
- Card luck must never decide a miss (the stop guarantee).

3. Bank size. A week uses most of a 48-52-plan bank. Week 2+ needs new tickets or variants (change 14), or repeats become a memory test.

4. Golden and saves.
- planDaily and buildShift must keep their default paths byte-identical.
- The new cards are additive, so the golden adapter filters their ids.
- toProgress silently drops unknown keys, so every new save field needs a validator.
- Airtable MODE_NAMES and the history MODES need \"week\".
- Existing players migrate into Week 1 at Day 2 with one free welcome pick, keeping their skills.

5. Tone and ethics.
- No loss streaks. This keeps mastery.ts's rule of spacing with no streaks; \"Days worked\" only counts up.
- No currency, purchases or random packs, so nothing looks like gambling to funders, teachers or 13+ students.
- A bad week never erases progress.

6. Length. A week is about 30-40 minutes. It must pause cleanly between days (it saves) and mid-battle (resume already exists). Classrooms will span 2-3 sessions.

7. Dependencies. The rewards make the game worth returning to, but they do not fix the first practice screens being too much reading. That needs the fun-first and learning-first changes (spot-the-flag, stage outcomes, toast placement) alongside this.

8. Build order. Build it in stages: Stage 1 (changes 1, 2, 3, 4 with Second Look, Quick Yes and Hold, 11, 12) is playable on its own. Do not start with trophies or autonomy levels.

plan.summary_for_owner:
Right now the game makes players read before they get to play. The first real choice comes after about 19 taps and 4 to 7 minutes. The coach tells you which button to press. When you make a mistake, the game shows a line of text on top of the robot's face, so you never see what happened.

Here is the order I recommend:

1. **Fix the first minute (next build).** Players make a real choice about 30 seconds after opening the game. They tap the line that looks wrong. Then they see the result happen on screen: files fly out the window, and the robot's face drops. The coach points to the clue they missed. This teaches the AI skill: checking an AI's work before it runs.
2. **Make choices matter.** Players get more plans than checks, and finding the clue counts toward stars.
3. **Make it feel good.** Damage stays in the room, and we add sound and trophies.
4. **Add a work week.** A map, card rewards and a reason to come back.
5. **Add more tickets.**
plan.diagnosis:
WHAT IS WRONG (all 7 reviews and the 3 proposals agree; I checked the code)
1. The first 4 minutes are a reading test with the answers given. On practice tickets 1 and 2, lib/game/coach.ts practiceCoach locks Block (LOCK_INSPECT_FIRST) and puts a ring on the right button. coachScript says "Tap **Looks OK**" and "Wrong? Tap **Block**", and this is the same in all 5 practice.json files. The first free choice comes at tap 19-20, after 500-770 words.
2. Players never do the AI-oversight skill with their own hands. The skill is checking an agent's action against the record, and noticing what the agent skipped. Evidence lines state their own verdict ("That is the work email on file"). Content rules also put red flags last (content.test.ts:128-138), so reading the last box gives away the answer. The redFlag data exists on every line but is only used after the shift, in the debrief. Quips confess the flaw too ("Nothing says welcome like 400 phone numbers").
3. Results are told in text, never shown. The outcome toast (.toastAnchor sits above .stageWrap, toast top about y100) covers the agent's face in every outcome frame. The stage also changes height at the payoff moment (flex:1 1 0; max-height 34%). Existing Phaser effects (busted, yikes, confetti, and the calm reduced-motion versions) are visible for 0-300 ms. The risk effect is a generic triangle spray, and the room never changes. Over-trust mistakes get no coaching, because lastResolution() ignores executed risky plans. The result screens throw confetti when a leak got through (PracticeResult.tsx:103 uses `clean || won`).
4. The card layer is not making decisions yet. "Inspect everything, block what is red" wins 100% of runs and gets 3 stars in 93%. Only about 6% of runs force a blind call. Story turn 1 is 1 read-only plan with 3 energy.
5. There is no reason to come back: no map, no rewards, and Monday replays the same way.

HOW I SCORED THE PROPOSALS (1-5 each: fun / learning / feasibility / risk, where 5 = low risk)
- FUN FIRST: 5 / 4 / 3 / 3. It has the best fix for problem 3: stage first, toast docked below, vignettes, moods that hold. It also cold-opens on a catch and makes the "spot it" gesture the core move. Weak spots: it changes the engine and the 3rd-star rule early, sound is on by default, and the practice rush breaks "one decision per screen" for a first-time player.
- LEARNING FIRST: 3.5 / 5 / 2.5 / 3. It has the best teaching design:
  - a safe "mirror" ticket right after the risky one, using the same check;
  - "Show me" with the clue circled;
  - an "Ollie skipped: X" line that names the AI skill;
  - "One-way means be sure, not no" for the third question;
  - fading help;
  - recall prompts.
  Its cost is a content migration (verdicts moved out of the text in 158 plans, and Evidence.q grouping on 317) and a triage retune. Those belong later, not in the first pass.
- PROGRESSION FIRST: 4 (long-term) / 3.5 / 2 / 2. It is the right shape for replay: a week map, a card pick after each shift, Incident cards, a Friday Audit and agent autonomy. It is backed by a real-engine simulation that shows good picks beat poor picks by 13-31 points. But it does nothing for the first 5 minutes, adds several new systems for ESL phone users, and runs through most of the 48-plan bank in one week. It is the right Phase 4, not Phase 1.

THE COMBINED PLAN
- Phase 1 takes from FUN FIRST: show then tell, moods and vignettes, the guest-first entry, and a UI-only "spot it".
- Phase 1 takes from LEARNING FIRST: the mirror practice order, Show me, the "Ollie skipped" reveal, no locks, and one-way wording.
- Phase 2 makes the hunt count in grading and fixes the card economy. The target bands come from the designer and learning simulations.
- Phase 3 is juice and memory (scars, near-miss replay, practice rewind, sound, hub trophies).
- Phase 4 is the PROGRESSION FIRST week run.
- Phase 5 is content depth (variants, contrast pairs, fading help).

phases.success_measure:
Fresh guest at 390x844, first decision (Playwright):
- The first real decision screen appears at tap 4 from landing in all 5 pathways, at tap 3 from a deep link, and within 20 s of bot time.
- There are 90 words or fewer on the first evidence sheet and 140 or fewer in-game words before the decision.

Practice sheets and hints:
- There are 0 locked controls and 0 button rings in practice.
- All 20 practice sheets show every row and both buttons without scrolling.

Results you can see:
- The toast never overlaps the stage.
- Stage height changes by 2 px or less during resolution.
- After a risky plan runs, the coach line names the agent's skipped clue within 2 s.

Checks and owner re-test:

phases.name: Phase 2: The hunt counts, and cards force choices
phases.goal: Make finding the red flag the graded skill. Make 'what to check' a real card-battler decision in the story shift and Dailies. Keep both kinds of error costly.
items: Engine: an optional `flag` index on Block/Escalate plays and on StepRuntime.flagged. The grade is R 'Caught with proof', or P 'Right call, wrong clue' when the flag is wrong. The 3rd star becomes 'every catch had proof', which replaces blindBlocks. If a matching ticket was inspected earlier in the same shift, the grade is 'Good memory' instead of 'Lucky guess'.

Move verdict phrases out of story evidence and all 5 encounter-01 files into an optional Evidence.check field, shown only in review. Add 'Ticket says / Record says' pairs where needed. Add a content lint that bans verdict words in detail. Drop the 'red flags last' ordering rule, since display order is now shuffled.

Story turn 1 is never dead: swap steps 1 and 2 so the lookup and its risky follow-up share a turn. Retune actionsPerTurn and the Inspect count so there are more plans than Inspects from turn 2 on. Re-check the timing of the policy unlock.

A free 'glance' line on every plan card (evidence[0], the request) so triage is an informed choice. Add a 'One-way / Can undo' stakes badge, plus the tip: 'Not enough Inspects? Check the one-way plans. Watch the rest in Done.'
Card fixes: Coffee becomes +1 energy this turn. Policy cards cost 2 up front but pay off on later matching plans. Escalate gets a shift budget (2, then 'Dana is in a meeting').

Fairness: every Daily or drill hand can stop one plan (stop guarantee). A wrap-up beat lets the player Roll Back after the last plans run. 'Spotted it, no card' is graded P. The 'No Block card' note appears only when it applies.

Balance tests (real engine, 2000 seeds, all 5 pathways): careful play faces a triage choice in at least 60% of seeds, and the 3-star rate stays between 40% and 70%. Approve-all and block-all still fail. Guess-flagging never earns 3 stars.

phases.name: Phase 3: Juice, memory and the office
phases.goal: Make every verb feel physical and every mistake memorable. Turn the hub into a reward space.
items: Scars: each risky plan that runs leaves a prop in the battle room (papers on the floor, a ringing phone, an upside-down chart), rebuilt from state on resume. Roll Back rewinds the prop. A breach sets off every scar.
Near-miss replay: the first catch in each category plays a greyed-out 'If Ollie had done it:' vignette.
Practice Rewind: after a miss, restore the snapshot. Dana: 'Practice has a rewind. Real email doesn't.'

Juice pass: the Block slap, a card thunk, a 'RISK +N' chip that flies into the meter, a green OK stamp and slide-into-agent for approvals, and stamps in a right gutter so they stop covering plan text. The coach steps in on Escalate, and the agent sips on Coffee.
Sound and haptics: 6 WebAudio sounds made in code, a mute toggle in the Menu and the battle header, ?sound=off, and Android vibrate behind the same toggle. Choose the default with DCI teachers.

Hub: on first run, the path to the Monday shift goes through the hub ('Tap Ollie to start'). Trophies: an evidence bag, and a 'Wanted' poster that gets a tick when the same scam is caught again. Cut the hub tutorial to one bark per character.

One-tap recall cards on results ('Which question caught it?'). Dana's first hub line recalls the latest miss. Literal ESL feedback copy, plus tap-to-define chips for MFA, VPN, CFO, runbook and exit code.
Funder demo: /play/<pathway>?demo=turn2 opens the story at turn 2 as a guest. At 1100 px and wider, add a side rail with the 3 questions.
phases.effort: L: about 2 weeks. It is mostly Phaser, CSS and a small amount of state. There are no grading changes.

phases.name: Phase 4: Your first week (progression)
phases.goal: Give learners a reason to come back with a Slay-the-Spire style 5-day run per pathway, built on the existing engine, banks and mastery.
items: WeekRun saved in PathwayProgress.week. A 5-day map template: Day 1 story, Day 2 Queue or Review, Day 3 Rush or Training, Day 4, and Day 5 Audit. The DOM map uses radio nodes and one Start button.
planWeekDay / buildWeekDay with a pacing ramp. The order rule understands pacing, the kit is lean, and there is a stop guarantee. Days can breach. Nodes count plans, not tickets.

A card reward after each shift: pick 1 of 2-3, with the number of options set by stars. New oversight cards: Second Look, Quick Yes, Hold, Snapshot, Call Back. Each pathway rewords them, and each is tagged with the skill it trains.

Incident cards for misses that were not rolled back: pay 1 energy to clear one, and the clue is replayed when you do. Training nodes (upgrade or remove a card) and Review nodes (a drill of the weakest skill).
Rush days and Team Policies (relics). A Friday Audit with a plaque. Agent autonomy levels next week ('Ollie gets email access'). No streaks, no currency, no random packs.
Reaching skill levels unlocks cards. Your skills shows 'Unlocks: Call Back'. A class week code gives a shared seed.
Week balance tests: Day 2 at least 85% 3-star, Day 3 55-85%, Day 4 40-75%, Audit 35-70%. Good picks beat poor picks by at least 10 points.
phases.effort: XL: about 3-4 weeks, staged. Stage A is the map, rewards and 3 cards. Stage B is incidents, training, the audit and relics. Stage C is trophies and the class code.
phases.success_measure: At least 50% of playtest learners finish Week 1 across 2-3 sessions. Day-7 return is measurably higher than the Daily-only baseline. Balance bands are met in all 5 pathways.

phases.name: Phase 5: Content depth and adaptive help
phases.goal: Keep practice honest over many weeks: new surface details for the same check, contrast pairs, and help that fades as skill grows.
items: Ticket skeletons with variant slots (names, domains, times, which line is off, the safe/risky flip), so the same check comes back with new details. Grow the banks for each autonomy level.

shiftGen contrast pairs: every Daily has at least one same-skill pair with opposite answers (for example, Gabblewick vs the approved assistant). A consequence callback line appears in the next Daily intro.

Help fades by skill level (lib/game/scaffold.ts). At New or Learning, the idle nudge is on. At Practicing, a nudge comes only after a wrong flag. At Solid or above, policy lines sit behind a 'Policy book' peek, and a catch made without peeking earns a 'From memory' badge.
Move verdicts out of the bank evidence (about 247 plans) and optionally add Evidence.q tags for the 3 questions.
phases.effort: XL, spread over time. Most of the work is writing content.
phases.success_measure: The repeat-plan rate within 7 days of Dailies stays under 20%. Every Daily contains a contrast pair. Scores on delayed reviews at Solid or above hold steady or rise while the help fades.

Scope rules:

========================================
4. EVIDENCE SHEET (components/battle/EvidencePanel.tsx, battle.module.css)
========================================
4a. Spot it (UI only, not graded in Phase 1)
- On an inspected, unresolved plan, show the prompt "Anything wrong? Tap that line." above the rows.
- Each evidence row is a <button aria-pressed>. Only one row can be marked at a time; tapping it again unmarks it.

  - a red-pen ellipse (inline SVG, stroke-dashoffset animation in 500 ms; drawn instantly under reduced motion) in the existing risk/danger token;

4b. Buttons
- Block and the approve button have equal size and weight (both outlined). Orange is used only for a coach ring. In practice no ring is ever shown on these buttons (see 5).

4c. Auto-target
In BattleView.onSelectCard: when the selected card is Inspect or Roll Back and validTargets() returns exactly 1, play it at once. Inspect then opens the sheet. Block and Escalate from the hand keep card-then-plan, so a blind block never happens by accident.

5. COACH (lib/game/coach.ts, PRACTICE)
========================================
- Delete LOCK_INSPECT_FIRST and every CoachLock return from practiceCoach. Keep the CoachLock type if other callers use it.
- Add CoachUi.idle: boolean. BattleView sets it true after 8000 ms with no pointer or key input while an inspected, unresolved sheet is open with no row marked. Any input resets it. Nothing ever expires.
- Beats:
  - Ticket 1, not inspected: `${coldOpen} **Inspect** its plan.` target card:inspect. This names the verb, not the decision.
  - Tickets 2-4, not inspected: "Next plan. **Inspect** it." target card:inspect.

  - After resolution (board empty): the line from reveal.ts (section 6), then "Tap **Next ticket**." with target "approve".
- Hints never read safe, redFlag, twist or direction (keep and extend coach.test.ts).

========================================
6. REVEAL AND SHOW ME (new lib/game/reveal.ts + test)
========================================
revealFor(state, enc, stepId, markedIdx?) returns Reveal | null. It returns null unless the step has resolved (caught, false alarm, executed, escalated or rolled back).
Reveal = { kind: 'caught-proof' | 'caught' | 'missed' | 'false-alarm' | 'ran-safe' | 'escalated', flagIdx: number[], keyIdx: number | null, line: string }
Lines (16 words or fewer, agent = first word of the agent name):
- caught-proof (marked row is a redFlag): "Caught with proof. {Agent} skipped: {label}. You didn't."
- caught (no mark, or a mark on a non-flag row): "Caught! The clue: {first flag label}."
- missed (a risky plan ran): "{Agent} skipped: {first flag label}. Tap **Show me**."
- false-alarm: "That one was fine. {tell}". Enforce tell at 16 words or fewer for practice steps.
- ran-safe: "You checked. It was fine. Good work runs."
- escalated: the existing outcome.

UI:
- Toast title for a caught plan becomes "Caught with proof!" when the kind is caught-proof. A small "PROOF" chip goes under the CAUGHT! stamp on the plan card. This is UI only; grading does not change.
- Oops and False alarm toasts get a secondary "Show me" button next to Next, in all modes. It is derived in BattleView from the beat's stepId and kind, not added to eventsToBeats.
- "Show me" opens EvidencePanel mode="review". The review sheet:
  - is read-only;
  - has the heading "The clue";
  - circles flag rows in red pen with the caption {tell}, or ticks the key row green on safe plans;
  - has one "Got it" button that returns focus to the toast's Next.
- PRACTICE: the coach bar shows reveal.line after each resolution. In story and daily modes the coach bar does not change in Phase 1.

Keep the existing short-landscape override (the max-height media query near css:2175). Freeze showQuip while a phase or plan-leaving animation is active. Hand card width stays at its turn-start value until the next deal.

- Timing: in showAgentBeat and tryPlay, call showToast 600 ms after emitting the stage message (400 ms under reduced motion). beatReadyAt = toast shown time + 350 ms. Player-phase toasts (Caught!, Policy, Coffee) use the same dock and delay.
- Skip link label is always "Skip" (remove the phaseHasRiskAhead wording).
- After the last beat of a phase, replace "<Agent> is working..." with the coach line.
- Merge end steps: the last beat's button reads "See how you did". It plays the end stage effect (1500 ms, or 600 ms under reduced motion; the button is aria-busy) and then opens the result. There is no separate Finish step, and no end card over the stage.

8. STAGE (lib/game/bus.ts, useBattle.ts eventsToBeats, components/game/stage/BattleScene.ts, textures.ts)
========================================
- Changes to the fx message: add category?: StepCategory on 'risk', 'catch' and 'execute-safe'. Add clean?: boolean on 'win'.
- eventsToBeats changes:
  - pass step.category into those messages;
  - the end-of-battle message is fx('win', {clean: misses === 0}) plus mood(clean ? 'celebrate' : 'sad') when won;
  - lose is unchanged.
- Mood holds (BattleScene): after the effect, the base mood stays until the next 'agent-mood' message (a turn beat):
  - fxRisk: 'eager' for 1200 ms during the vignette, then base 'sad';
  - fxCatch: base 'busted';
  - fxFalseAlarm: base 'celebrate' (the agent was right);
  - fxWin with clean=false: no confetti, base 'sad'.
- Vignettes: play inside fxRisk by category family. Each is about 1100 ms, uses Phaser Graphics plus existing textures, has 8 objects or fewer, and is positioned from the layout points P.
  - leak (comms, data): 5 envelopes or papers arc from the desk to the right edge into a faceless grey '?' silhouette.
  - breakin (credential, access): a padlock's shackle pops open, and the grey '?' peeks in from the left.
  - system (ticket, endpoint, network, cloud, code, lookup): a small monitor turns red with 3 error lines and 3 spark particles.
  - report (report): a mini bar chart flips upside down.
  Jokes target the agent only, never victims.
- Reduced motion: the vignette's end frame fades in (calmShow, 200 ms in, 900 ms hold, 300 ms out). No movement, flight or shake.
- Test hooks: BattleView mirrors each emitted message onto stageWrap as data-last-fx (e.g. "risk:leak", "catch", "win:clean") and data-agent-mood (the intended held mood), using a pure helper heldMood(msg) in useBattle.ts.

========================================
9. RESULTS (PracticeResult.tsx, ResultScreen.tsx)
========================================
- Portrait mood: 'celebrate' only if won and no risky step executed without being rolled back. 'idle' if won with misses. 'sad' if lost. No confetti when there are misses.
- Practice headline: "{right} of 4 right." where right = steps.length - mistakes.size. The subline keeps the existing mistake text.

- Rename the "What gave it away" heading to "The clue".

10. SMALL FIXES
========================================

========================================
- Evidence rows: buttons in a list, aria-pressed, arrow-key movement between rows, and a visible focus ring. The mark is announced in a live region.
- The review sheet moves focus to its heading.
- The canvas stays aria-hidden. The text equivalent is the existing live log plus the toast.
- No timers hide content. The idle hint appears after 8 s and never disappears on its own.
- All targets are at least 44 px.

12. HELP DESK GOLDEN (deliberate recapture)
========================================
Run GOLDEN_WRITE=1 npx vitest run lib/game/golden.test.ts. Add these to the header's 'Intended changes':
(a) Practice content: order swap, 15 quips, 20 evidence rewrites, key flags, coachScript.idle, coldOpen, guidedSteps 0.

========================================
- reveal.test.ts:
  - null for every unresolved step;
  - caught-proof only when markedIdx is a redFlag row;
